result.summary: The environment features a vast, unmarked paved area adjacent to residential buildings, lacking basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crosswalks or traffic controls. While a sidewalk exists on one side, the wide expanse of asphalt creates a long, unprotected crossing distance with poor visibility due to parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide, unmarked expanse of asphalt requires pedestrians to cover a long distance without any protection or refuge.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs, signals, or markings are present to regulate vehicle flow or prioritize pedestrian movement.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: A long row of parked cars obscures the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the paved area

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and crossing locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Road Diet
interventions.description: Add lane markings to organize traffic and narrow the travel lanes, which naturally reduces vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with sidewalks and a curb ramp featuring tactile paving, indicating basic pedestrian infrastructure. However, the lack of marked crosswalks and the presence of parked cars near the intersection create visibility hazards, and a large blurred area significantly limits the overall assessment.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sightlines between pedestrians at the corner and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a pedestrian crossing area at this intersection despite the presence of a curb ramp.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian path and alert drivers to the crossing location.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The intersection lacks basic pedestrian safety features such as marked crosswalks, stop signs, or ADA-compliant curb ramps. A tall wall on the right creates a significant blind spot, obstructing sightlines between pedestrians and vehicles.

hazards.name: Blind Corner

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection lacks stop signs or traffic signals, leading to unpredictable vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven road surface with accumulated debris can cause tripping hazards or affect vehicle braking.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk constrained by a high retaining wall and a continuous line of parked vehicles. There is a total absence of marked crossings, traffic calming, or pedestrian-oriented infrastructure, creating a high-risk environment for mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles along the sidewalk edge obscures pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers, making mid-block crossings dangerous.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway, adjacent to the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian movements across the travel lanes.
